title: The Gupta Age: India's Classical Golden Age

questions.question: The Gupta era begins with the coronation of Chandragupta I in which year?
questions.rationale: Chandragupta I's coronation year 319-320 CE marks the start of the Gupta era; he took the title maharajadhiraja after marrying the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi.

questions.question: The Allahabad (Prayag) Prashasti, the main source for Samudragupta's conquests, was composed by:
questions.rationale: Harisena, Samudragupta's court poet, composed the Prayag Prashasti, listing uprooted northern kings and reinstated southern vassals.

questions.question: Which Viceroy-era historian called Samudragupta the 'Indian Napoleon'?
questions.rationale: Vincent Arthur Smith, using the conquests of the Prayag Prashasti, described Samudragupta as an 'Indian Napoleon'.

questions.question: The Chinese pilgrim who visited India during Chandragupta II's reign was:
questions.rationale: Fa-Hien travelled c. 399-414 CE during Chandragupta II Vikramaditya's rule; Xuanzang came later, under Harsha.

questions.question: Aryabhata, born in 476 CE, is credited in the Aryabhatiya with:
options: Explaining eclipses as shadows and stating the earth rotates
questions.rationale: The Aryabhatiya explains place value with zero, treats eclipses as shadow effects, states the earth rotates, and gives pi as 3.1416.

questions.question: The rust-free Iron Pillar of Delhi was erected during the reign of:
questions.rationale: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar, standing rust-free for over 1,500 years, is credited to Chandragupta II Vikramaditya — a monument to Gupta metallurgy.

questions.question: The Nalanda mahavihara was founded by:
questions.rationale: Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda, which grew into the era's greatest university, later praised by Xuanzang.

questions.question: The Gupta empire's western collapse was caused by invasions of the Hunas led by:
questions.rationale: After Skandagupta repelled the first Huna wave, Toramana and his son Mihirakula broke the western empire in the early sixth century.

questions.question: Harsha's biography, the Harshacharita, was written by his court poet:
questions.rationale: Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita, the biography of Harsha of Thanesar (606-647 CE), and the novel Kadambari.

questions.question: The Aihole inscription of Ravikirti (634-635 CE) celebrates which victory of Pulakeshin II?
options: Defeat of Harsha on the Narmada
questions.rationale: The Chalukya court poet Ravikirti's Aihole inscription praises Pulakeshin II for halting Harsha's southern march on the Narmada.
